claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating has an FCC crystal structure.
The initial coating has high lattice distortion.
The coating process produces a high density of pre-existing dislocations and stacking faults.
At 300 K, the FeNiCrCoCu coating has stable wear resistance and high elastic modulus.
At 300 K, FeNiCrCoCu has high stacking-fault energy.
High stacking-fault energy favors planar dislocation glide and work hardening in this coating.
Planar glide and work hardening maintain a stable oxide layer and high wear resistance at 300 K.
The stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrCoCu decreases as temperature increases.
The temperature-induced decrease in stacking-fault energy lowers the critical stress for deformation twinning.
Deformation twins initially enhance strength but subsequently increase local strain localization.
At approximately 450–500 K, thermal energy overcomes the lattice-distortion barrier in FeNiCrCoCu.
Above the critical temperature, rapid dislocation multiplication and annihilation cause breakdown of the FCC lattice into a disordered, softened state.
Elevated-temperature CoCrFeMnNi loses structural integrity and consequently undergoes a sharp increase in wear rate.
Frictional heating raises the local contact temperature, promotes HEA softening, and increases wear.
Frictional heating can raise the FeNiCrCoCu flash temperature above the proposed disorder threshold and accelerate the transition.
When the local contact temperature exceeds approximately 475 K ±25 K, wear rate will increase by more than 50% and elastic modulus will decrease.
The elastic modulus of the coating at 300 K is approximately 100–120 GPa.
Composition changes that induce a BCC phase, such as Al addition, will alter the threshold and deformation mechanism.
Higher applied loads lower the critical temperature because they increase flash heating.
Near the proposed transition, dislocation density should peak and then rapidly decrease as lattice disorder develops.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies 475 K ±25 K, whereas the uncertainty field states that the same threshold may vary by ±50 K and that the transition may be spread across a 50 K interval.

The predicted outcome defines an approximately fixed local-contact critical temperature, while the boundary field says higher load lowers the critical temperature because of flash heating. Increased flash heating can lower the required ambient temperature, but does not by itself establish that the local-temperature threshold changes.

The hypothesis groups dynamic recrystallization and amorphization as forms of rapid lattice disorder, although dynamic recrystallization produces new crystalline grains and is not equivalent to amorphization or breakdown into an atomically disordered state.
